newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Teva mulls European generic partner.
newsitem.headline: Teva mulls European generic partner.

text.p: Israel's Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd is considering forming a marketing alliance with a global company to distribute its generic drugs in Europe, an official said on Sunday.
Teva's chief financial officer, Dan Suesskind, said the company would decide at the end of the quarter whether to market its products alone in Europe or seek a partnership.

"There are talks with more than one global company about a partnership. We would bring the generic know-how and the licencing and they would bring the name and the distibution," Suesskind told Reuters.

Teva, Israel's biggest pharmaceutical company and one of the biggest generic drug companies in the United States, is now seeking to build its European generics business. In the last year it has acquired companies in Italy, Hungary and Britain.
"Our intention is to be a leader in Europe when the generics market really picks up," said Suesskind.

In a related development, Suesskind said he expected British approval for Teva's Copaxone multiple sclerosis treatment in the next quarter. In December, the company won approval from the U.S. Food and Drug Administration to market the drug in the United States.
